chapters.part: Foundations of Claude and AI Fluency
chapters.title: What Claude Is, and Isn't
chapters.tease: Claude is not a product, a chatbot or an app, and confusing the three layers is the fastest way to fail a question.

chapters.part: Foundations of Claude and AI Fluency
chapters.title: The Model Family
chapters.tease: Three sizes, one decision that sets your cost, latency and ceiling in a single call: which model do you reach for?

chapters.part: Foundations of Claude and AI Fluency
chapters.title: Tokens, Context, and the Budget Nobody Reads
chapters.tease: Treating context as free is like booking a table for six and hoping it seats twelve.

chapters.part: Foundations of Claude and AI Fluency
chapters.title: Pricing as a Design Constraint
chapters.tease: Pricing is not a footnote to architecture; it is the architecture, and the exam wants you pulling three levers at once.

chapters.part: Foundations of Claude and AI Fluency
chapters.title: Capabilities and Limitations
chapters.tease: The gap between what Claude does impressively in a demo and what it does reliably at scale is where systems get built badly.

chapters.part: Foundations of Claude and AI Fluency
chapters.title: The Constitutional Mindset
chapters.tease: When Claude refuses, the professional does not jailbreak; they ask why, add context, or hand the decision to a human.

chapters.part: Foundations of Claude and AI Fluency
chapters.title: Reading the API Reference Like an Architect
chapters.tease: If your code never inspects the stop reason, you have a latent bug, and the exam has a question that will find it.

chapters.part: Foundations of Claude and AI Fluency
chapters.title: AI Fluency: The Four Cs
chapters.tease: Four skills, four failure modes, and an exam that asks you to match each scenario to the right one.

chapters.part: Foundations of Claude and AI Fluency
chapters.title: Delegation as Design
chapters.tease: Most systems delegate too little where volume lives and too much where the stakes live, and the exam wants you to spot the mismatch.

chapters.part: Foundations of Claude and AI Fluency
chapters.title: The Architect's Stance
chapters.tease: Every exam question is secretly a stance question, and the answer a senior engineer would sign on a Monday morning wins.

chapters.title: Anatomy of a System Prompt
chapters.tease: If your system prompt is one big paragraph, you have a bug, even when the output looks fine.

chapters.title: The Instruction Hierarchy
chapters.tease: A user cannot override your system prompt by asking, but a search result can inject instructions if you let it.

chapters.title: Few-Shot Examples That Actually Teach
chapters.tease: Three diverse examples beat ten similar ones, and one well-chosen edge case beats five safe ones.

chapters.title: Chain-of-Thought That Earns Its Tokens
chapters.tease: Step-by-step reasoning improves hard answers, taxes easy ones, and should never be shown raw to a customer.

chapters.title: Extended Thinking and the Budget
chapters.tease: Turn extended thinking on everywhere and six weeks later your bill is four times what it should be.

chapters.title: Prefilling the Assistant Turn
chapters.tease: A single opening brace in the assistant turn guarantees JSON more reliably than a paragraph of pleading.

chapters.title: Temperature and the Determinism Illusion
chapters.tease: Temperature zero does not make Claude deterministic, and the exam is really testing whether you know what to add.

chapters.title: Output Shaping: XML, JSON, and the Format Contract
chapters.tease: Free text, XML or JSON: the right choice depends on who consumes the output, and JSON everywhere is an over-commitment.

chapters.title: The Constraint-First Rule
chapters.tease: The chatbot did the thing it was told not to do. Look at where the rule sat in the prompt before you blame the model.

chapters.title: Debugging Prompts Like Code
chapters.tease: Prompts are code. If yours have no version, no diff, no tests and no logs, nobody on your team can safely change them.

chapters.title: What Claude Code Is
chapters.tease: Claude Code is not a chat that can touch files; it is an agent runtime in your terminal, and the exam treats it that way.

chapters.title: CLAUDE.md and the Persistence Hierarchy
chapters.tease: Two CLAUDE.md files disagree. Which wins? If you said the project one, you have already lost the point.

chapters.title: The Memory System — Four Types
chapters.tease: Four kinds of memory, four different lifecycles, and one rule: when memory disagrees with what you see, update the memory.

chapters.title: The Agent Loop
chapters.tease: Perceive, think, act, observe. When an agent misbehaves, the fix starts with naming which step broke.

chapters.title: Tool Use in Claude Code
chapters.tease: The agent used sed through Bash to edit a file. The fix is not a stricter Bash permission; it is Read then Edit.

chapters.title: Plan Mode
chapters.tease: Most bad edits come from incomplete understanding, not incompetence, and plan mode is the discipline that fixes it.

chapters.title: Task Tracking
chapters.tease: Finish five steps, then tick all five at once? You have just thrown away the only thing that made the list useful.

chapters.title: Permission Modes
chapters.tease: If the agent keeps asking to delete things, the answer is not to grant it permission; it is to ask why it wants to.

chapters.title: The Golden Path for a Session
chapters.tease: Seven moves make a good session, and the one everybody skips is the one that tells you whether the fix actually worked.

chapters.title: Slash Commands and the Skill Router
chapters.tease: A slash command is not interface decoration; it is the entry point to a skill, and the description is what routes it.

chapters.title: Hooks Are Shell Scripts, Not Agents
chapters.tease: A hook cannot call Claude, cannot use tools and cannot think. Ask it to make a judgement call and it will fail.

chapters.title: Writing a Pre-Tool Hook
chapters.tease: Under twenty lines of shell, and writing it once teaches you the whole hook contract.

chapters.title: Skills and the YAML Frontmatter
chapters.tease: The router cannot match on vibes. A description that says does xyz-related things is genuinely useless to it.

chapters.title: MCP Server Config in settings.json
chapters.tease: A bare token in a committed settings file is a secret on disk, in git, forever. Move it out.

chapters.title: Worktrees for Isolated Work
chapters.tease: A worktree is a parallel universe for your repo: experiment freely, and if nothing comes of it, it cleans itself up.

chapters.title: Working with GitHub via gh
chapters.tease: Shipping broken because CI was red is the exam's canonical GitHub failure. Checks first, merge second.

chapters.title: Sandboxed Permissions
chapters.tease: Most engineers grab shell access to understand a codebase. Read-only was the right sandbox all along.

chapters.title: Context Hygiene at Compaction
chapters.tease: Twenty turns in, the agent forgot a file was off limits. The model is not the problem; the constraint lived in the wrong place.

chapters.title: Subagents from the CLI
chapters.tease: Find where the retry logic lives? Explore. Should we move to queues? Plan. Build the whole feature? General-purpose.

chapters.title: Debugging Claude Code Itself
chapters.tease: When a session behaves inexplicably, do not guess. Restart it with verbose logging and repeat the failing task.

chapters.title: The Agent Loop, Formalised
chapters.tease: Read state, reason, act, observe, repeat until no tool is called. That is the whole pattern; everything else is decoration.

chapters.title: Orchestrator and Worker
chapters.tease: The agent got confused halfway through. Before touching the prompt, ask whether one agent is carrying the whole job alone.

chapters.title: Subagents and Context Isolation
chapters.tease: A subagent gets fresh context. One sentence, the most tested fact about subagents, and the reason they work at all.

chapters.title: Tool vs. Subagent: The Decision
chapters.tease: Get the user's most recent order sounds like it needs an agent. It is a database lookup. It is a tool.

chapters.title: Parallel vs Sequential Tool Calls
chapters.tease: Twenty files to read means one response with twenty calls, not twenty rounds. Unless one of them depends on another.

chapters.title: Briefing a Subagent
chapters.tease: A one-line brief for a fifteen-minute task produces garbage, and the fix is engineering, not nicer writing.

chapters.title: Trust But Verify
chapters.tease: The subagent said it updated the config. The file is unchanged. Whose fault is the architecture?

chapters.title: Long-Running Agents
chapters.tease: The agent hung for an hour and nobody knows what it cost. That sentence is a professional failure, not bad luck.

chapters.title: Multi-Agent Choreography
chapters.tease: Three agents where one would do, and coordination keeps breaking. The answer is usually to collapse to one.

chapters.title: Failure Modes of Agentic Systems
chapters.tease: Given a symptom, name the failure mode and the structural fix. Improve the prompt is the beginner's answer.

chapters.title: Why MCP Exists
chapters.tease: Every model times every data source is a custom integration. MCP turns that multiplication back into addition.

chapters.title: Host, Client, Server
chapters.tease: Claude Code is the MCP server, right? No. It is the host, it contains a client, and it talks to servers.

chapters.title: Tools, Resources, and Prompts
chapters.tease: A tool that just reads a file is a resource in disguise, and exposing it as a tool wastes every round trip.

chapters.title: JSON Schema as the Contract
chapters.tease: The model never sees your tool's source code. It sees the description, and the description decides whether it ever gets called.

chapters.title: stdio vs SSE Transport
chapters.tease: Stdio is simpler, so a candidate picks it for a shared cloud service. Simpler and wrong, because the transport must match where the capability lives.

chapters.title: Building an MCP Server in TypeScript
chapters.tease: Return a bare string from a tool handler and the SDK fails silently. Memorise the content block shape.

chapters.title: Building an MCP Server in Python
chapters.tease: The server hangs under concurrent requests. Somewhere in an async handler there is a blocking call.

chapters.title: Authenticating an MCP Server
chapters.tease: We skipped auth for simplicity is a sentence the exam treats as an automatic failure.

chapters.title: Error Handling with Structured JSON
chapters.tease: Invalid argument is a dead end. Must be one of open, closed or all, got active is a retry waiting to happen.

chapters.title: When Not to Reach for MCP
chapters.tease: A dozen half-configured servers that fired once and never again. Every untouched boundary is cost you pay for nothing.

chapters.title: The Anthropic SDK, End to End
chapters.tease: The most common first-call error is a system prompt in the messages array. That is the other vendor's shape, not this one.

chapters.title: Streaming with Server-Sent Events
chapters.tease: If the next step is parse this JSON and act, streaming saves you nothing. Save it for a human watching tokens land.

chapters.title: The Batch API
chapters.tease: Half price for anything that can wait a day. It is the biggest cost lever you have without touching a prompt or a model.

chapters.title: Prompt Caching, in Depth
chapters.tease: Caching enabled, hit rate zero. Diff two consecutive prefixes and you will find the timestamp that is quietly killing it.

chapters.title: File Uploads and Persistent Documents
chapters.tease: A hundred-page PDF the user will ask ten questions about should be uploaded once, not shipped with every request.

chapters.title: Citations
chapters.tease: Asking the model to cite in brackets gives you citations that look right and prove nothing. The API gives you character offsets.

chapters.title: Cost Ledgers
chapters.tease: The bill tripled overnight. Is the answer a query, or a guess? The ledger decides which.

chapters.title: Latency Budgets
chapters.tease: The team optimised the model for a week. The five tool calls per turn were the bottleneck all along.

chapters.title: Model Routing by Cost
chapters.tease: Routing everything to Opus because it is the best is paying a senior architect to answer the phones.

chapters.title: Rate Limits and Retries
chapters.tease: Retrying a bad request five times wastes time and money. It will fail identically every time.

chapters.title: Projects and Persistent Instructions
chapters.tease: A Project for every conversation is misuse. A Project for a workflow you repeat is the whole point.

chapters.title: The Five Artifact Types
chapters.tease: A diagram is an SVG artifact, not a React component with an SVG inside. Trust the obvious answer.

chapters.title: Skills as YAML-Fronted Invocables
chapters.tease: A skill that only works after three other skills have run is not a skill; it is a fragile dependency waiting to fail silently.

chapters.title: Writing Skill Descriptions the Router Loves
chapters.tease: Summarise a GitHub PR is a description that routes on vibes. The strong version names what to do, when, and when not.

chapters.title: Plan Mode as Discipline
chapters.tease: The agent broke production doing something unexpected. The fix is not be more careful; it is a read phase before the write.

chapters.title: The Task Tool as External Memory
chapters.tease: Should remember is a phrase that means will forget. The fix is externalising the state, not hoping.

chapters.title: Context Isolation as a Discipline
chapters.tease: Your primary session feels sluggish and forgetful. That is not a reason for a new session; it is a reason to delegate harder.

chapters.title: Connectors and the Data Boundary
chapters.tease: A support bot that can send email as the chief executive is a phishing attack in a box. Minimum permissions, always.

chapters.title: Sharing a Project
chapters.tease: This rule is annoying, delete it. Repeat across a team for a year and the shared Project no longer resembles its design.

chapters.title: The Artifact Refactoring Loop
chapters.tease: The AI wrote it and nobody can find where it lives. That is what happens when a chat becomes the home of production code.

chapters.title: Evals That Beat Vibes
chapters.tease: It seems better is not a change management strategy. Twenty to fifty cases built in an afternoon is.

chapters.title: Building a Regression Suite
chapters.tease: A bug fix that ships without a new eval case has fixed today's symptom, not the class of bug.

chapters.title: Red-Teaming Your Own System
chapters.tease: Your system will be red-teamed eventually, by users, adversaries or researchers. The only question is whether you found the failures first.

chapters.title: Harm-Reduction Patterns
chapters.tease: We have a strong filter, we do not need the other layers. The filter will fail, and then you have shipped the harm.

chapters.title: PII and Data Minimisation
chapters.tease: We sent everything just in case is a professional error. The model rarely needs the sensitive fields to do the job.

chapters.title: Logging and Tracing
chapters.tease: The bot gave me the wrong answer three hours ago. Can you replay exactly what happened, or are you guessing?

chapters.title: The Cost Dashboard
chapters.tease: When the finance director asks why the bill tripled, the answer should be a query, not an investigation.

chapters.title: Drift Detection
chapters.tease: Nobody touched the prompt and it got worse anyway. That is drift, and it is the architect's silent enemy.

chapters.title: Incident Response for AI Systems
chapters.tease: The system starts producing wrong output at three in the morning. The first move is not to investigate. It is to freeze.

chapters.title: The Continuous Improvement Loop
chapters.tease: Ship, measure, learn, ship again. Systems inside this loop mature; systems outside it quietly rot.

chapters.title: The Exam's Shape
chapters.tease: Scenario questions dominate, time is tight, and a brilliant Claude Code candidate can still fail on the MCP section.

chapters.title: The Five Domains, Revisited
chapters.tease: One answer is structurally correct and two sound plausible but are the beginner's move. Trust the structural fix.

chapters.title: Top 12 Exam Tips
chapters.tease: Fifteen facts on an index card the day before, re-read the morning of, and most ambiguous scenarios resolve themselves.

chapters.title: The Ten Anti-Patterns
chapters.tease: Spot one anti-pattern in a scenario and look for the others. They cluster, and the one that fits is usually the answer.

chapters.title: What to Memorise vs Reason
chapters.tease: Memorise everything and you run out of time. Reason everything and you miss the numbers. The trick is a few anchors and a method.

chapters.title: Day-Of Strategy
chapters.tease: Perfectionism during a timed exam is how good candidates fail. You are trying to pass, not to be right on everything.

chapters.title: Life After the Badge
chapters.tease: I just certified is a status update. I just certified, and here is the repo showing what I ship, is a career move.

chapters.title: The Community
chapters.tease: Success stories get likes. Failure stories get respect, and they are where the field is actually being invented.

chapters.title: The Next 12 Months
chapters.tease: The material that got you certified in 2026 will need updating by 2028. The badge is a starting point or a decay curve.

chapters.title: The Architect Who Ships
chapters.tease: On the day after you pass, nothing changes about your ability. What changes is the responsibility. So ship one small thing.
